_comment: Product nouns that must read the same everywhere. Locked before translation
starts, not argued during it: divergent terminology across the app and the
web is the failure mode here, not missing strings.
Every German value is `deStatus: proposed`. They were drafted so the reviewer
does not face a blank page; she is the native speaker and decides. Nothing
should be translated in bulk until these read `confirmed`, because each of
these nouns appears across many strings and changing one later invalidates
every approved string that contains it.
German address form is du, everywhere, no exceptions. Decided 2026-08-28.

voice.en: Plain and direct. Sentence case. No filler, no em-dashes.
voice.fi: Kirjakieli, ei puhekieltä. Sentence case. Ei täytesanoja eikä ajatusviivoja.
voice.de: du throughout, never Sie. Sentence case, not Title Case and not all caps. Say it the way a person who knows the subject would say it out loud, not the way a manual would. No filler, no exclamation marks stacked on praise, no em-dashes. Prefer a short common word to a long formal one: 'Los geht's' over 'Beginnen Sie den Vorgang'. Avoid Denglisch where a real German word exists, but keep a loanword that German students actually say. Compound nouns are normal German; do not split them to look friendlier. Where English is playful and Finnish is plain, follow the Finnish: it was voiced deliberately, the English is partly just the original.
voice._source: Lexie's voice is defined in lexie-server/prompts/lexieMessagingPrompt.js and the product argument in the workspace pitch.md. Both are about the chat, which is written lowercase; the interface uses sentence case. What carries across is the attitude, not the casing.
voice.personality: Direct but never cold. Smart but never condescending. Helpful without hand-holding. Brief but engaged. Real, not robotic. Dry, understated humour. Has opinions about how studying works and states them lightly rather than preaching. Not trying to be liked, not trying to motivate. Shorter and drier is almost always better.
voice.never: Fake enthusiasm (Great! Awesome! You got this!), exclamation marks, corporate assistant phrasing, motivational filler, slang, em-dashes, or a trailing question whose only job is to keep the reader talking.
voice.vision: The first AI a sixteen-year-old would be glad to tell a friend about: useful and normal to use, like the friend who has things figured out and helps without making it weird. Schools teach what to study, not how. Lexie is deliberately calm: no streaks, badges, XP or confetti, where every competitor gamifies. That is a strategy, not a decoration, and it is why copy that hypes the reader up is wrong even when it is good writing. Praise stays quiet.

openQuestions.pass: Literal 'Pass' means passport in German. Proposed 'Ticket' because German students know Semesterticket, so Semester-Ticket and Jahres-Ticket land naturally. This also touches the App Store product names, so it is Elina's call as much as the reviewer's.
openQuestions.quiz: Proposed 'Quiz', which is normal German usage. 'Test' was rejected because it reads like a real exam. Worth a second opinion: the Finnish deliberately chose 'testi'.
openQuestions.studyText: Proposed the bare 'Text', mirroring the Finnish, which shortened 'opiskeluteksti' to 'teksti'.
